title: Tlos Ruins, Yakapark & Saklıkent Gorge: Fethiye Inland Day Circuit
seoTitle: Tlos, Yakapark & Saklıkent Gorge: 2026 Fethiye Day Loop
metaDescription: Combine Lycian Tlos ruins, Yakapark trout lunch, and icy Saklıkent Gorge in one day from Fethiye or Kalkan. 2026 fees, water shoes, and timing.
quickAnswer: Start at Tlos Ancient City around 08:30 while the exposed acropolis is cool, drive 10 minutes uphill to Yakapark for a shaded trout lunch beside mountain springs, and finish inside Saklıkent Gorge during afternoon heat. Expect icy Taurus snowmelt, pack strapped water shoes and a dry bag, and budget 7–8 hours round trip.

body.text: How do you combine Lycian Tlos acropolis, trout lunch at Yakapark and Saklıkent Canyon?

Visit Tlos first at 08:30–09:00 before midday sun hits the hillside, continue 5 kilometres up to Yaka village for a shaded trout lunch at Yakapark around 11:30–12:30, and enter Saklıkent Gorge at 13:30–14:00 when its 300-metre limestone walls provide natural shade and cool canyon air.

Listed on UNESCO’s World Heritage Tentative List since 2009, Tlos preserves Lycian rock tombs, a Roman theatre, stadium, Great Bath, and an Ottoman-era hilltop fortress; [Turkish Museums](https://www.turkishmuseums.com/museum/detail/2194-mugla-tlos-archaeological-site/2194/4) lists 2026 non-Turkish admission at €3 (summer hours 08:30–19:30, winter 08:30–17:30). Running the loop in this sequence also avoids the noisy jeep-safari convoys that crowd Saklıkent’s entrance mid-morning.
How cold is the water inside Saklıkent Gorge in summer?

Saklıkent’s water stays bracingly cold all summer because it rises from underground karst springs fed by Taurus Mountain snowmelt. Even when Fethiye coast temperatures pass 35°C in July and August, stepping into the initial waist-deep river crossing feels genuinely icy—roughly 10–13°C—before shallower upstream pools warm slightly under filtered light.

According to [GoTürkiye](https://goturkiye.com/fethiye/saklikent-canyon), Saklıkent Canyon runs 18 kilometres long and up to 300 metres deep, with roughly 4 kilometres walkable after April once spring melt subsides. Visitors who prefer staying dry can walk the suspended wooden boardwalk bolted to the cliff wall as far as the main spring lookout, then relax on timber platforms above the river with gözleme or grilled trout.
What water shoes and dry bags are needed?

Bring closed-toe rubber-soled water shoes with secure ankle straps and a 5–10 litre roll-top waterproof dry bag. Flip-flops snap or wash away immediately in the fast entrance current, and bare feet slip on wet limestone cobbles and silt-coated boulders once you wade past the wooden boardwalk.
Pack these essentials for the full inland loop:

items: Strapped water shoes or neoprene reef booties (basic plastic shoes are also sold or rented at the Saklıkent gate, though personal fit is far safer).
Waterproof phone pouch on a lanyard plus a roll-top dry bag for car keys and cash.
Quick-dry shorts and a spare dry T-shirt left in the car for the drive back.
Breathable sun hat and 1.5 litres of water for the exposed morning walk at Tlos.
Turkish lira cash for national park parking, small village stalls, and Yakapark refreshments.

body.text: How long does the full circuit take from Fethiye or Kalkan?

Plan 7 to 8 hours door-to-door from either Fethiye or Kalkan, including driving, unhurried ruin exploration, lunch, and two hours inside Saklıkent Gorge. Driving from Fethiye to Tlos takes roughly 45 minutes (about 45 km), while Saklıkent sits about 40–50 km east of Fethiye and 45 minutes inland from Kalkan.

faq.q: Can you walk inside Saklıkent Gorge in winter or early spring?
faq.a: No. Between November and April, winter rains and Taurus snowmelt swell the river, making the canyon floor impassable. Usually only the dry suspended boardwalk remains accessible until water levels drop.

faq.q: Is the initial river crossing at Saklıkent safe for children?
faq.a: The first 20-metre crossing past the boardwalk has a strong, icy current guided by a fixed rope. Young children and unsteady walkers should stay on the wooden boardwalk and spring terrace rather than crossing.

faq.q: Do I need to book Yakapark in advance for lunch?
faq.a: On weekdays outside August, walk-in tables under the trees are usually easy to find, especially before 12:30. On summer weekends, arriving by 11:45 avoids waiting behind tour groups.

faq.q: Can you visit Tlos and Saklıkent by public dolmuş?
faq.a: Seasonal dolmuş minibuses run from Fethiye bus station to Saklıkent, and separate local routes serve Yaka village, but connecting all three stops by public transport wastes hours waiting. A rental car or private driver is far more practical.

faq.q: What is the entrance fee for Tlos Ancient City in 2026?
faq.a: Turkish Museums lists non-Turkish visitor admission at €3 for ages 8 and above, while Turkish citizens can use MüzeKart. Always check current seasonal hours before setting out.

faq.q: Are lockers available at Saklıkent Gorge?
faq.a: Yes, small paid lockers sit near the canyon entrance before the boardwalk, though leaving valuables locked out of sight in your vehicle trunk and carrying only essentials in a dry bag is simpler.
